title: Arrays & Python lists
syllabusDesc: Store ordered items, index quickly, and resize as needed.
desc: Python lists are dynamic arrays: they keep elements contiguous in memory, giving O(1) average time for indexing and append, with O(n) inserts/removes in the middle.
placeholder:
# Add, update, and slice
nums = [10, 20, 30]

# your code here
solution:
nums = [10, 20, 30]
nums.append(40)
nums.insert(1, 15)
nums[2] = 25
print("list:", nums)

# slice copy
first_two = nums[:2]
print("first two:", first_two)

# remove last
last = nums.pop()
print("popped:", last)
print("after pop:", nums)
techniques: When to copy vs mutate a list
challenges: Reverse a list without using list.reverse()
Merge two sorted lists into one sorted list
notes:
Indexing is O(1); inserting in the middle is O(n) because elements shift.

Lists keep insertion order and allow duplicates.
